newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM vows secular education reforms will go on.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM vows secular education reforms will go on.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz vowed on Wednesday to push through secularist education changes despite violent street protests by Islamists.
"The government is completely committed to carrying out the education reforms," Yilmaz told a news conference.
Police using dogs, water cannon and batons on Tuesday broke up a large Islamist demonstration in Ankara against plans to curtail religious high schools.
Yilmaz said he would not bow to Islamist strong-arm tactics.
"They are mistaken if they think they can intimidate the republic's government with streets protests, threats and blackmail," he said.
Yilmaz, a conservative, came to power in June after Islamist predecessor Necmettin Erbakan resigned under pressure from the secularist army.
